# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Righteous and the Sinner Before God

---

**3:1** Why dost thou sleep, O my soul,
and not bless the LORD?

**3:2** Sing a new song to God,
who is worthy to be praised;
sing and be glad of heart, those who honor him.

**3:3** The LORD teaches the righteous ones
when he disciplines them;
the life of the righteous is in the instruction of the LORD.

**3:4** Our God is compassionate and merciful,
and he pardons [sinners] and saves.

**3:5** The righteous man stumbles and the LORD justifies him;
he falls and watches for what God will do for him.

**3:6** He searches where [correction] will come from for him,
he looks intently to God.

**3:7** The righteous man does not spare his soul
when he makes atonement for his unintentional sin;

**3:8** he cleanses the inward soul from shame;
he looks [intently] to the LORD for the sin of ignorance,

**3:9** that it may not be reckoned to him as a sin,
lest the enemy trample upon him.

**3:10** The sinner stumbles and curses his life,
the day of his birth and the birth pangs of his mother.

**3:11** He adds sins upon sins in his life;
he falls — and evil is his fall — and he shall not rise.

**3:12** The destruction of the sinner is forever,
and he will not be remembered when God visits the righteous.
This is the portion of sinners forever.
But those who fear the LORD will rise to eternal life,
and their life will be in the light of the LORD, and will not fail.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Greek (Codex Vindobonensis). Hyphenated compounds preserve construct chains. Bracketed words [thus] are implied by grammar but absent from the surface text.*
